label: Vāta
title: Vāta
html:
Description: The principle of mobility and movement, primarily composed of Ākāsha and Vāyu

Function: Regulates nerve impulses, breathing, heart pulsation, and muscle movement. Governs sensory perception and elimination

Gunas: ruksha, laghu, shīta, khāra, sūkshma, chala, vishada

Physical Attributes: Characterized by a thin and light frame, dry, rough, and cold skin, kinky, brittle, and scarce hair, small, recessed, and active eyes, and irregular and variable appetite and elimination

Psychological Attributes: In balance, promotes joy, creativity, and flexibility. Out of balance, creates fear, anxiety, insecurity, and restlessness

Season: Dominant in Sarad/ Hermanta, characterized by dry, light, and cold qualities

Time of Day: Maximum activity during dawn and dusk, specifically 2:00 to 6:00 AM and PM

Agni: Vishama Agni, irregular digestive fire, fluctuating metabolism often accompanied by gas, bloating, and indigestion

Koshtha: Krūra Koshtha, characterized by dry, hard stools and a strong tendency toward constipation

Nādi: Sarpa Gati, moves like a snake or cobra. Feels superficial, cold, fast, and feeble, typically 80–95 beats per minute

Important to Know: Governs the later years of life, age 50+

Main Sites: mūrdhni, asthi, srotra, pakvāshaya, kati, sakthi, tvak, kesha

label: Pitta
title: Pitta
html:
Description: The principle of transformation and metabolism, primarily composed of Agni and Āpas

Function: Governs digestion, absorption, and assimilation, maintains body temperature and complexion, and is responsible for intelligence and understanding

Gunas: ushna, tīkshna, laghu, drava, sara, snigdha

Physical Attributes: Characterized by a medium frame and steady weight. The skin is soft, warm, and oily. The hair is straight and shiny with a tendency toward graying. The eyes are sharp and penetrating. The appetite is strong and unbearable if delayed

Psychological Attributes: In balance, promotes understanding, logic, bravery, and intelligence. Out of balance, arouses anger, hatred, jealousy, and sharp judgment

Season: Dominant in Grishma, characterized by hot, sharp, and bright qualities

Time of Day: Maximum activity during midday and midnight, specifically 10:00 to 2:00 AM and PM

Agni: Tīkshna Agni, sharp digestive fire, intense metabolism with a desire for large quantities of food and a tendency toward acidity

Koshtha: Mrudu Koshtha, characterized by soft, oily, or loose stools and regular bowel movements

Nādi: Mandūka Gati, moves like a jumping frog feels full, bounding, forceful, and hot, typically 65–80 beats per minute

Important to Know: Governs adulthood, age 16 to 50

Main Sites: sādhaka, lasīka, sveda, rakta, hirdayam, vasā, tvak, nābhi, grahani, yakrut, plīhā, pittasha, drig, āmāshaya

label: Kapha
title: Kapha
html:
Description: The principle of structure and cohesion, primarily composed of Āpas and Pruthivī

Function: Forms the body's bulk and shape; provides the lubrication for joints and organs; maintains immunity and cellular memory

Gunas: guru, manda, shīta, snigdha, slakshna, sandra, mrudu, sthira, picchila, kathina, sthūla, drava

Physical Attributes: Characterized by a large, strong, and well-developed frame; skin is thick, pale, cool, and oily. The hair is thick, plentiful, and wavy. The eyes are large, lovely, and sweet. Appetite and digestion are slow and steady

Psychological Attributes: In balance, expressed as love, compassion, calmness, and forgiveness. Out of balance, leads to attachment, greed, possessiveness, and depression

Season: Dominant in Hermanta/ Vasanta, characterized by wet and cool qualities

Time of Day: Maximum activity during early morning and early evening, specifically 6:00 to 10:00 AM and PM

Agni: Manda Agni, slow digestive fire, dull metabolism with poor appetite and a tendency to gain weight even on a normal diet

Koshtha: Madhyama Koshtha, balanced, characterized by healthy, well-formed stools and regular, effortless elimination

Nādi: Hamsa Gati, moves like a swimming swan, feels deep, slow, wavy, broad, and cool, typically 50–65 beats per minute

Important to Know: Governs childhood from birth to age 16

Main Sites: shira, sandhi, shushumna jala, shleshaka, granthi, āmāshaya, jihva, rasa, gandha, nasā, kloma, phuphusa
